questions.question: Use the picture of square tables in a row to explain the rule times 2, plus 2.
questions.expected_answer: Each table has one person on its top side and one on its bottom side, which is 2 per table. There is also one person at each end of the row, which is 2 more. So seats = tables × 2 + 2.

questions.question: How many square tables in a row are needed for 62 guests? Work backwards and check.
questions.expected_answer: Undo plus 2: 62 − 2 = 60. Undo times 2: 60 ÷ 2 = 30 tables. Check: 30 × 2 + 2 = 62.

questions.question: Show that add 1, then double gives the same seats as double, then add 2, for 1, 2 and 3 tables.
questions.expected_answer: For 1 table, 2 × 2 = 4 and 1 × 2 + 2 = 4; for 2 tables, 3 × 2 = 6 and 2 × 2 + 2 = 6; for 3 tables, 4 × 2 = 8 and 3 × 2 + 2 = 8. They match every time, so the rules are equivalent.
